questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my french and also move far away to experience living somewhere new without the ability to just go back to Denmark to visit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university is very good at sending you new information, and otherwise there are a lot of people to ask at the facilities themselves

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received e-mails but I was also lucky to have a friend going abroad there as well, who arrived earlier than me. I arrived two weeks after the start of the semester and therefore missed the introduction programs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I used facebook marketplace where a lot of people post appartments. The hard part was sometimes not being able to write a message due to rules about being in another country, but this could be fixed by using a VPN. I even moved a short while after coming to Montreal due to personal reasons, and finding a room while here was really easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's the best. Getting to know people outside of the study life was crucial for me to really experience the city. I spent most of my time with other people than students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find the different subjects you want and then you sign up. Really easy. You can even change after trying your course out for two weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Catalogues and descriptions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are like me and want to spent a lot of time outside of the university, choose subjects in the 200 category. They are quite chill.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course levels were a bit easier than at KU, but I also intentionally chose lower levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Different in terms of exams because I both had multiple choice question exams and oral exams.
It was very much pen and paper in the classes I took.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
French oral communication
French written communication
Human Development in a Life Span
Canadian History Post-Confederation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The french courses were nice as to use the language on a daily basis and the history course was nice to understand the context of the society I was living in. Very interesting all in all.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Trips with the university to hikes and other cultural experiences

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables were soooo expensive. Almost cheaper to eat junk food than cook yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were an international club for exchange students but I didn't go very much.
There's also a gym connected to the uni, but I was very full.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Going to concerts! There is so much happening in this city every day.
Also hiking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Concerts, hiking and going to restaurants

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Montreal feels like the european gateway to North America and everybody speaks english as well as french.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of people. I went so many places by my self and always ended up talking to somebody.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Use the city and try everything at least once
2. Take advantage of the beautiful mountain in the middle of the city
3. Organize to meet up with the people you talk to. Everybody is so nice and wants to connect

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring warm clothes if you're doing a winter semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a new city and getting a new perspective of distance. So many people in Montreal are from around the world so you really get to know a lot of different cultures in one.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Wanting to go back :3

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
